description: This dataset gives 15-minute screened air temperature and humidity from sensors in the urban canyons around the Roger Stevens cooling pond on the University of Leeds campus and at nearby sites in central Leeds. It was collected with sensors from the National Centre for Atmospheric Science at the University of Leeds and published on Data Mill North; the early portion was described by Peterson, Iuorio, Berretta, Hassall and Cooper at the SEEDS 2018 conference. Onset HOBO Pro v2 sensors were mounted about 2 m up on signposts, and one 3 m up a tree at Mill Hill Chapel, recording temperature, relative humidity and dew point; the record reports that on a hot afternoon in June 2019 campus sites were up to 2 degrees warmer than the chapel base site. Coverage: the Leeds campus and city-centre sites, 2018 and 2019. Access: CSV files per sensor and year from Data Mill North. Licence: not stated on the data.gov.uk entry; free. Caveats: no accuracy guarantee, and some sensors were knocked loose or wetted for periods. Simulation uses: validating microclimate models of street canyons and the cooling effect of water features. Related records: the Vienna water features case study and the Sydney urban form data.
